docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> UgridDataset | Network1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Network1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: ESMF — unstructured-mesh NetCDF
docs.text:
The ESMF reader. ESMF (the Earth System Modeling Framework) stores its unstructured mesh as NetCDF with an explicit node list and element connectivity: node coordinates in nodeCoords (shape nodeCount × coordDim, column 0 longitude and column 1 latitude), the per-element node table in elementConn (elementCount × maxNodePElement), and numElementConn giving each element's real node count. The driver builds the surface mesh — the node list becomes the nodes and elementConn the fill-padded, mixed-degree face connectivity. Read through the vendored GDAL multidimensional API (no declared dependency).

Driver name esmf Suffixes .nc Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns UgridDataset

An ESMF mesh is not UGRID, so read_file reaches the driver through its NetCDF-suffix fallback:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("ne4np4-esmf.nc")
mesh.mesh.n_node          # the ESMF node list
mesh.mesh.n_face          # the ESMF elements

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The real node count comes from numElementConn, not from a fill value. Each element keeps its first numElementConn nodes; the rest of the row is padding and becomes -1 fill, so a mesh of triangles and quads yields a fill-padded, mixed-degree table without depending on the file's own pad value.
  • elementConn is 1-based by default. A start_index attribute overrides the base; the connectivity is resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a writer.
  • Coordinates are carried in the file's unit, degrees by default. A units attribute on nodeCoords naming radians is honoured and the coordinates converted to degrees; otherwise they are left as the file gave them.
  • No CRS. The mesh is lon/lat on a sphere with no EPSG authority, so crs is None rather than guessed.
  • Only the topology is read. The element areas and other ESMF fields are not shipped as variables; this driver declares read_mesh only.

Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for ESMF unstructured-mesh NetCDF.

The nodes come from nodeCoords (column 0 longitude, column 1 latitude) and the 1-based elementConn table is re-based and fill-padded into mixed-degree face connectivity. numElementConn gives each element's real node count, so a triangle in a wider table keeps its first three nodes and the rest of the row becomes fill.

Documented limitations
  • The real node count comes from numElementConn, not from a fill value. Each element keeps its first numElementConn nodes; the rest of the row is padding and becomes -1 fill, so a mesh of triangles and quads yields a fill-padded, mixed-degree table without depending on the file's own pad value.
  • elementConn is 1-based by default. A start_index attribute overrides the base; the connectivity is resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a writer.
  • Coordinates are carried in the file's unit, degrees by default. A units attribute on nodeCoords naming radians is honoured and the coordinates converted to degrees; otherwise they are left as the file gave them.
  • No CRS. The mesh is lon/lat on a sphere with no EPSG authority, so crs is None rather than guessed.
  • Only the topology is read. The element areas and other ESMF fields are not shipped as variables; this driver declares read_mesh only.
Example

Read an ESMF mesh (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real NetCDF file), reached through read_file's NetCDF fallback::

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("ne4np4-esmf.nc")
mesh.mesh.n_node          # the ESMF node list
mesh.mesh.n_face          # the ESMF elements

class EsmfDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for ESMF unstructured-mesh NetCDF.

    The nodes come from ``nodeCoords`` (column 0 longitude, column 1 latitude) and the
    1-based ``elementConn`` table is re-based and fill-padded into mixed-degree face
    connectivity. ``numElementConn`` gives each element's real node count, so a triangle
    in a wider table keeps its first three nodes and the rest of the row becomes fill.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The real node count comes from ``numElementConn``, not from a fill value.**
          Each element keeps its first ``numElementConn`` nodes; the rest of the row is
          padding and becomes ``-1`` fill, so a mesh of triangles and quads yields a
          fill-padded, mixed-degree table without depending on the file's own pad value.
        - **``elementConn`` is 1-based by default.** A ``start_index`` attribute overrides
          the base; the connectivity is resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a
          writer.
        - **Coordinates are carried in the file's unit, degrees by default.** A ``units``
          attribute on ``nodeCoords`` naming radians is honoured and the coordinates
          converted to degrees; otherwise they are left as the file gave them.
        - **No CRS.** The mesh is lon/lat on a sphere with no EPSG authority, so ``crs``
          is ``None`` rather than guessed.
        - **Only the topology is read.** The element areas and other ESMF fields are not
          shipped as variables; this driver declares ``read_mesh`` only.

    Example:
        Read an ESMF mesh (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real NetCDF file),
        reached through ``read_file``'s NetCDF fallback::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

            mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("ne4np4-esmf.nc")
            mesh.mesh.n_node          # the ESMF node list
            mesh.mesh.n_face          # the ESMF elements
    """

    name = "esmf"
    long_name = "ESMF unstructured mesh"
    suffixes = (".nc",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is an ESMF mesh, by its defining arrays.

        Keyed on ``nodeCoords``, ``elementConn`` and ``numElementConn``, which together
        are unique to ESMF, so a plain NetCDF or another model's ``.nc`` -- SCRIP, GEOS,
        MPAS, ICON, 3Di or TUFLOW FV -- is not claimed. Opening a non-NetCDF file raises
        inside GDAL and is reported as "not ESMF" rather than propagated.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when all three defining arrays are present.
        """
        with gdal.ExceptionMgr(useExceptions=True):
            try:
                dataset = gdal.OpenEx(path, gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER | gdal.OF_READONLY)
            except RuntimeError:
                return False
            try:
                names = _group_names(dataset.GetRootGroup())
            finally:
                dataset.Close()
        return {_NODE_COORDS, _ELEMENT_CONN, _NUM_ELEMENT_CONN} <= names

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read an ESMF mesh into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ESMF ``.nc`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- this driver reads only the topology, which is eager.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: The node list and the fill-padded, mixed-degree face
                connectivity.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If a defining array is missing.
        """
        return _EsmfReader(path).build()

docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> UgridDataset | Network1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Network1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Esri TIN — directory of .adf files
docs.text:
The Esri TIN reader. An Esri TIN is a directory of big-endian binary .adf components, not a single file. Read through plain binary parsing and the vendored GDAL for the projection (no declared dependency).

Driver name esri_tin Suffixes .adf Capabilities read_mesh, read_data Extra required none Returns UgridDataset

A directory has no suffix, so read_file cannot dispatch a bare directory path. Reach the driver either way:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

# point at any .adf component of the TIN
mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("path/to/tin/tdenv9.adf")

# or pass the directory with an explicit driver
mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("path/to/tin", driver="esri_tin")

elevation = mesh.get("node_z")

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The input is a directory of .adf files. read_file reaches it through any .adf component, or through driver="esri_tin" on the directory. A raster .adf (an Esri GRID), whose directory has no triangle table, is declined.
  • Masked triangles are dropped. The convex-hull frame triangles flagged in tmsk.adf are excluded, so the mesh is the surface the TIN represents; the frame nodes they referenced stay in the node list, unreferenced.
  • Triangle indices are 1-based — resolved to 0-based, the base recorded for a writer. Every face is a triangle; Esri's clockwise triangles are reversed to counter-clockwise.
  • The projection is read from prj.adf. The Esri-dialect WKT is morphed from Esri form; it resolves to an EPSG code when one is named, else the normalised WKT, else None — never a guess.
  • Node elevation (tnz.adf) becomes a node_z variable.

docs.title: pyramids_mesh.drivers.esri.EsriTinDriver
docs.text:
Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the Esri TIN directory format.

An Esri TIN is a directory of big-endian .adf files. The driver reads the node coordinates and elevations, the 1-based triangle table, and the mask that marks the convex-hull frame triangles the TIN carries but does not treat as surface -- it keeps only the unmasked triangles, exactly as the stored kept-count records.

Documented limitations
  • The input is a directory of .adf files. read_file cannot dispatch a bare directory (it has no suffix), so point it at any of the TIN's .adf files, or pass the directory with driver="esri_tin". can_open accepts either and confirms the TIN components are present; a raster .adf (an Esri GRID), whose directory has no triangle table, is declined.
  • Masked triangles are dropped. The hull-frame triangles flagged in tmsk.adf are excluded, so the mesh is the surface the TIN represents. The frame nodes they referenced stay in the node list, unreferenced.
  • Triangle indices are 1-based. They are resolved to 0-based and the base is recorded for a writer. Every face is a triangle.
  • The projection is read from prj.adf only when it validates. A missing or unparseable prj.adf leaves crs None rather than guessed.
  • Node elevation becomes a node_z variable.
Example

Read an Esri TIN by its directory path (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real TIN directory)::

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("path/to/tin_directory")
elevation = mesh.get("node_z")
Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/drivers/esri.py 
class EsriTinDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the Esri TIN directory format.

    An Esri TIN is a directory of big-endian ``.adf`` files. The driver reads the node
    coordinates and elevations, the 1-based triangle table, and the mask that marks the
    convex-hull frame triangles the TIN carries but does not treat as surface -- it keeps
    only the unmasked triangles, exactly as the stored kept-count records.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The input is a directory of ``.adf`` files.** ``read_file`` cannot dispatch a
          bare directory (it has no suffix), so point it at any of the TIN's ``.adf``
          files, or pass the directory with ``driver="esri_tin"``. ``can_open`` accepts
          either and confirms the TIN components are present; a raster ``.adf`` (an Esri
          GRID), whose directory has no triangle table, is declined.
        - **Masked triangles are dropped.** The hull-frame triangles flagged in
          ``tmsk.adf`` are excluded, so the mesh is the surface the TIN represents. The
          frame nodes they referenced stay in the node list, unreferenced.
        - **Triangle indices are 1-based.** They are resolved to 0-based and the base is
          recorded for a writer. Every face is a triangle.
        - **The projection is read from ``prj.adf`` only when it validates.** A missing or
          unparseable ``prj.adf`` leaves ``crs`` ``None`` rather than guessed.
        - Node elevation becomes a ``node_z`` variable.

    Example:
        Read an Esri TIN by its directory path (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a
        real TIN directory)::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

            mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("path/to/tin_directory")
            elevation = mesh.get("node_z")
    """

    name = "esri_tin"
    long_name = "Esri TIN"
    # An Esri TIN is a directory; read_file reaches it through any .adf component file.
    suffixes = (".adf",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "read_data"})

    def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether ``path`` is a TIN directory or an ``.adf`` file inside one.

        Overrides the base check, which declines every directory and only ever sniffs a
        file: an Esri TIN is a directory, reached either directly or through one of its
        ``.adf`` component files. Never raises -- a sniff error is warned and declined.

        Args:
            path: The filesystem path to test.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` for a TIN directory, or an ``.adf`` file whose directory is one.
        """
        tin_dir = self._tin_dir(path)
        if tin_dir is None:
            return False
        try:
            return self._sniff(tin_dir)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
            # Defensive: os.listdir on a readable directory does not raise, so this guard
            # mirrors the base class's never-raise contract rather than a reachable path.
            warnings.warn(  # pragma: no cover
                f"{self.name} failed to sniff {path!r} and is treated as declining it: "
                f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            return False  # pragma: no cover

    @staticmethod
    def _tin_dir(path: str) -> str | None:
        """Resolve the TIN directory from a directory or an ``.adf`` file path."""
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            return path
        if os.path.isfile(path) and path.lower().endswith(".adf"):
            return os.path.dirname(path)
        return None

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the directory holds the required TIN components."""
        present = {entry.lower() for entry in os.listdir(path)}
        has_required = all(component in present for component in _REQUIRED)
        has_header = any(header in present for header in _TDENV)
        return has_required and has_header

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a TIN into a :class:`ParsedMesh`, from its directory or an ``.adf`` file.

        Args:
            path: The TIN directory, or one of its ``.adf`` component files.
            lazy: Unused -- a TIN is small and read whole.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, node elevation and the unmasked triangle connectivity.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the path is not a TIN or a component is missing.
        """
        tin_dir = self._tin_dir(path)
        if tin_dir is None:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"{path!r} is not an Esri TIN directory or an .adf file inside one"
            )
        return _EsriTinReader(tin_dir).build()

Overrides the base check, which declines every directory and only ever sniffs a file: an Esri TIN is a directory, reached either directly or through one of its .adf component files. Never raises -- a sniff error is warned and declined.

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether ``path`` is a TIN directory or an ``.adf`` file inside one.

    Overrides the base check, which declines every directory and only ever sniffs a
    file: an Esri TIN is a directory, reached either directly or through one of its
    ``.adf`` component files. Never raises -- a sniff error is warned and declined.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` for a TIN directory, or an ``.adf`` file whose directory is one.
    """
    tin_dir = self._tin_dir(path)
    if tin_dir is None:
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(tin_dir)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Defensive: os.listdir on a readable directory does not raise, so this guard
        # mirrors the base class's never-raise contract rather than a reachable path.
        warnings.warn(  # pragma: no cover
            f"{self.name} failed to sniff {path!r} and is treated as declining it: "
            f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False  # pragma: no cover

docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> UgridDataset | Network1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Network1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Exodus II — finite-element mesh
docs.text:
The Exodus II reader. A .exo/.e file is NetCDF (CDF-2) underneath: node coordinates in coordx/coordy/coordz and one or more element blocks connect1/connect2/… whose rows are 1-based element-to-node lists carrying an elem_type attribute (QUAD4, TRI3, TETRA, …), with the block ids in eb_prop1. The NetCDF substrate is read through the vendored GDAL multidimensional API (no declared netCDF4 dependency, no exodus library).

Driver name exodus Suffixes .exo, .e Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns UgridDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("model.exo")
mesh.mesh.n_node, mesh.mesh.n_face

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Every element block's node list becomes a face row, including a volume element type such as TETRA. A genuine volumetric (3D) mesh is not modelled yet (design §21.1), so a tetrahedron's four node ids are read verbatim as a face rather than expanded into its bounding triangles; winding is then judged in the xy plane like any other face.
  • Connectivity is 1-based with mixed widths padded by 0 — a short row in a mixed-element table (triangles among quads) is padded with 0, never a valid 1-based id, and the normaliser rewrites it to -1 fill; the 1 base is recorded for a writer.
  • Results are not read — only the mesh is built; the per-timestep nodal and element variables an Exodus file may carry are out of scope for this reader.
  • coordz (a 3D file) contributes a node_z variable; a 2D file leaves it unset. There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None.

docs.title: pyramids_mesh.drivers.exodus.ExodusDriver
docs.text:
Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the Exodus II (.exo) finite-element mesh format.

The mesh comes from the node coordinates coordx/coordy (and coordz for a 3D file, carried as node_z) and the element blocks. Each block connectN is a 1-based element-to-node table tagged with an elem_type; every block's rows are concatenated into one face-node connectivity table, padded to the widest block so a mesh mixing triangles and quads is rectangular. The ids drop from 1-based to 0-based and the base is recorded for a writer; eb_prop1 and the per-element elem_type are carried as metadata.

Documented limitations
  • Every element block's node list becomes a face row, including a volume element type such as TETRA. A genuine volumetric (3D) mesh is not modelled yet (design section 21.1), so a tetrahedron's four node ids are read verbatim as a face rather than expanded into its bounding triangles; winding is then judged in the xy plane like any other face.
  • Connectivity is 1-based with mixed widths padded by 0. A short row in a mixed-element table is padded with 0 -- never a valid 1-based id -- and the normaliser rewrites it to -1 fill; the 1 base is recorded for a writer.
  • Results are not read. Only the mesh is built; the per-timestep nodal and element variables an Exodus file may carry are out of scope for this reader.
  • There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None.
Example

Read an Exodus mesh (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real .exo file), reached through read_file::

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("model.exo")
mesh.mesh.n_node, mesh.mesh.n_face

class ExodusDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the Exodus II (``.exo``) finite-element mesh format.

    The mesh comes from the node coordinates ``coordx``/``coordy`` (and ``coordz`` for a
    3D file, carried as ``node_z``) and the element blocks. Each block ``connectN`` is a
    1-based element-to-node table tagged with an ``elem_type``; every block's rows are
    concatenated into one face-node connectivity table, padded to the widest block so a
    mesh mixing triangles and quads is rectangular. The ids drop from 1-based to 0-based
    and the base is recorded for a writer; ``eb_prop1`` and the per-element ``elem_type``
    are carried as metadata.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Every element block's node list becomes a face row**, including a volume
          element type such as ``TETRA``. A genuine volumetric (3D) mesh is not modelled
          yet (design section 21.1), so a tetrahedron's four node ids are read verbatim as
          a face rather than expanded into its bounding triangles; winding is then judged
          in the ``xy`` plane like any other face.
        - **Connectivity is 1-based with mixed widths padded by ``0``.** A short row in a
          mixed-element table is padded with ``0`` -- never a valid 1-based id -- and the
          normaliser rewrites it to ``-1`` fill; the ``1`` base is recorded for a writer.
        - **Results are not read.** Only the mesh is built; the per-timestep nodal and
          element variables an Exodus file may carry are out of scope for this reader.
        - There is no CRS in the format, so ``crs`` is ``None``.

    Example:
        Read an Exodus mesh (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real ``.exo``
        file), reached through ``read_file``::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

            mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("model.exo")
            mesh.mesh.n_node, mesh.mesh.n_face
    """

    name = "exodus"
    long_name = "Exodus II"
    suffixes = (".exo", ".e")
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is Exodus II, by its coordinates, blocks and dims.

        Keyed on ``coordx`` plus a first element block ``connect1`` and the ``num_dim`` /
        ``num_nodes`` dimensions, so a plain NetCDF or another model's ``.nc``-style file
        is declined rather than misread.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the defining arrays and dimensions are present.
        """
        with gdal.ExceptionMgr(useExceptions=True):
            try:
                dataset = gdal.OpenEx(path, gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER | gdal.OF_READONLY)
            except RuntimeError:
                return False
            try:
                group = dataset.GetRootGroup()
                names = set(group.GetMDArrayNames())
                dimensions = _dimension_sizes(group).keys()
            finally:
                dataset.Close()
        if not {_COORD_X, f"{_CONNECT_PREFIX}1"} <= names:
            return False
        return _REQUIRED_DIMS <= set(dimensions)

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read an Exodus II file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.exo``/``.e`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- the mesh is read eagerly and the format carries no lazy
                results here; accepted to match the driver protocol.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: The surface mesh, ``node_z`` for a 3D file, and the block-id and
                element-type metadata.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file carries no element block.
        """
        return _ExodusReader(path).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
