            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Selafin / Serafin — TELEMAC
docs.text:
The TELEMAC Selafin reader, and the package's first binary driver. Fortran unformatted records with an undeclared byte order and an optional double-precision variant. It proves the lazy path: the topology and the one-float time records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a loader that seeks straight to it.

Driver name selafin Suffixes .slf, .srf, .ser, .sel Capabilities read_mesh, read_data, lazy_data, write_mesh, write_data Extra required none Returns UgridDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

dataset = UgridDataset.read_file("model.slf")
depth = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH").data   # read now; deferred until this line

dataset.to_file("copy.slf", driver="selafin")                 # lossless double precision
dataset.to_file("small.slf", driver="selafin", precision="single")  # smaller, lossy

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
The writer emits the same Fortran-record layout the reader parses, so a read → write → read round trip preserves the nodes, the connectivity (and its recorded 1-based IKLE base), the variable names and units, and the time steps.

  • Only node-located variables are written — the format has no face-located storage.
  • Every face must share a vertex count: Selafin stores a single element width (NDP), so a mixed tri/quad mesh is refused rather than written with a scrambled IKLE.
  • precision is "double" (the default — float64, a lossless round trip) or "single" (float32, smaller but lossy). A dataset with no face connectivity is refused.

docs.title: How it is read
docs.text:
• Byte order is detected, not declared. The first record must announce an 80-byte title in one order or the other; a file that does neither is not Selafin.
  • Precision comes from the title marker. SERAFIND is double precision, SERAFIN single, and the width applies to every float record — coordinates and data alike.
  • Variable names are 32 characters, split by position into a 16-char name and a 16-char unit. Splitting on whitespace instead would lose a multi-word name's tail.
  • IKLE connectivity is 1-based; it arrives 0-based, with the base recorded for a writer to restore.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable. IPARAM[2] and IPARAM[3] are the x and y origins the stored coordinates are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. Read without adding them, the mesh sits near zero instead of at its real location — plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the data to catch it.
  • A layered 3D file is refused. IPARAM[6] is the plane count; 0 and 1 both mean 2D, and a value above 1 is a real 3D file. Its NPOIN and prism IKLE cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning all planes' nodes under 6-node faces, and a faithful surface extraction needs a vendor file to verify the plane ordering, so it is refused rather than read as a malformed 2D mesh. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design §21.1).
  • A parallel sub-domain file is refused. A non-zero interface-point count (IPARAM[8]) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface points alone — the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for ordinary serial meshes. Merge the partitions before reading.
  • Variables are node-located, always — never inferred from an array length.
  • The IKLE row/column order could not be checked against a vendor file. It is read row-major (one element's NDP node ids contiguous), as the format specifies. A real file that stored it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is the detail a vendor sample should confirm, tracked for the vendor_data suite.
  • A partial final timestep is dropped with a warning — a run killed mid-write leaves a dangling time record, and only whole steps are read.
  • There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None; it is never inferred from the coordinate magnitudes.

Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the TELEMAC Selafin / Serafin format.

Fortran unformatted records whose byte order is not declared and is detected from the first record length (see :func:~pyramids_mesh._binary.detect_endianness). The file carries a mesh and node-located results over time, so the driver declares read_mesh, read_data and lazy_data: the topology and the one-float time records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a loader that seeks to it.

Documented limitations
  • The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable. IPARAM[2] and IPARAM[3] are the x and y origins the stored coordinates are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. A file with a non-zero origin read without adding it gives a mesh sitting near zero instead of in its real location -- plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the data to catch it.
  • Single versus double precision applies to every float record. The title's format marker (SERAFIND double, SERAFIN single) sets the width for the coordinates and every data slab alike; reading the wrong width desynchronises the file, which the trailing-length-word check then reports.
  • A layered 3D file is refused. IPARAM[6] is the plane count; 0 and 1 both mean 2D (some tools write 1 for 2D), and a value above 1 is a real 3D file whose NPOIN and prism IKLE cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning all planes' nodes under 6-node faces. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design section 21.1), so the file is refused rather than yielding a plausible, wrong mesh.
  • A parallel sub-domain file is refused. A non-zero interface-point count (IPARAM[8]) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface points alone -- the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for ordinary serial meshes, and keying on it would refuse them.
  • Selafin variables are node-located, always. The location is not inferred from an array length.
  • The IKLE row/column order could not be checked against a vendor file. It is read row-major -- one element's NDP node ids contiguous -- as the format specifies. A real file that stores it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is the detail a vendor sample should confirm.
  • There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None; it is never inferred from the coordinate magnitudes.

Examples:

  • Write the smallest valid Selafin file and read it back. The 1-based IKLE arrives 0-based, with the file's base recorded for a writer:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh.drivers.telemac import ( ... SelafinDriver, ... build_minimal_fixture_selafin, ... ) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf") ... build_minimal_fixture_selafin(path) ... dataset = SelafinDriver().read(path) dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (4, 2) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 3]] dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index 1

  • The one variable comes back node-located, with its time axis and the name and unit split from the 32-character record by position:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh.drivers.telemac import ( ... SelafinDriver, ... build_minimal_fixture_selafin, ... ) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf") ... build_minimal_fixture_selafin(path) ... dataset = SelafinDriver().read(path) ... variable = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH") ... location, shape, units = ( ... variable.location, ... variable.shape, ... variable.units, ... ) ... second_step = variable.data[1].tolist() location, shape, units ('node', (2, 4), 'M') second_step [1.5, 1.25, 1.75, 1.125]

class SelafinDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the TELEMAC Selafin / Serafin format.

    Fortran unformatted records whose byte order is not declared and is detected from the
    first record length (see :func:`~pyramids_mesh._binary.detect_endianness`). The file
    carries a mesh and node-located results over time, so the driver declares
    ``read_mesh``, ``read_data`` and ``lazy_data``: the topology and the one-float time
    records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a
    loader that seeks to it.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable.**
          ``IPARAM[2]`` and ``IPARAM[3]`` are the x and y origins the stored coordinates
          are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. A file with a
          non-zero origin read without adding it gives a mesh sitting near zero instead
          of in its real location -- plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the
          data to catch it.
        - **Single versus double precision applies to every float record.** The title's
          format marker (``SERAFIND`` double, ``SERAFIN`` single) sets the width for the
          coordinates and every data slab alike; reading the wrong width desynchronises
          the file, which the trailing-length-word check then reports.
        - **A layered 3D file is refused.** ``IPARAM[6]`` is the plane count; 0 and 1 both
          mean 2D (some tools write 1 for 2D), and a value above 1 is a real 3D file whose
          ``NPOIN`` and prism ``IKLE`` cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning
          all planes' nodes under 6-node faces. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh
          model pyramids does not have yet (design section 21.1), so the file is refused
          rather than yielding a plausible, wrong mesh.
        - **A parallel sub-domain file is refused.** A non-zero interface-point count
          (``IPARAM[8]``) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity
          would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface
          points alone -- the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for
          ordinary serial meshes, and keying on it would refuse them.
        - **Selafin variables are node-located, always.** The location is not inferred
          from an array length.
        - **The IKLE row/column order could not be checked against a vendor file.** It is
          read row-major -- one element's ``NDP`` node ids contiguous -- as the format
          specifies. A real file that stores it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is
          the detail a vendor sample should confirm.
        - There is no CRS in the format, so ``crs`` is ``None``; it is never inferred
          from the coordinate magnitudes.

    Examples:
        - Write the smallest valid Selafin file and read it back. The 1-based ``IKLE``
          arrives 0-based, with the file's base recorded for a writer:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.telemac import (
            ...     SelafinDriver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin(path)
            ...     dataset = SelafinDriver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (4, 2)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 3]]
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index
            1

        - The one variable comes back node-located, with its time axis and the name and
          unit split from the 32-character record by position:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.telemac import (
            ...     SelafinDriver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin(path)
            ...     dataset = SelafinDriver().read(path)
            ...     variable = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH")
            ...     location, shape, units = (
            ...         variable.location,
            ...         variable.shape,
            ...         variable.units,
            ...     )
            ...     second_step = variable.data[1].tolist()
            >>> location, shape, units
            ('node', (2, 4), 'M')
            >>> second_step
            [1.5, 1.25, 1.75, 1.125]
    """

    name = "selafin"
    long_name = "TELEMAC Selafin / Serafin"
    suffixes = (".slf", ".srf", ".ser", ".sel")
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset(
        {"read_mesh", "read_data", "lazy_data", "write_mesh", "write_data"}
    )

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is a Selafin file, by the endianness probe.

        The first record must declare an 80-byte title in one byte order or the other.
        That probe is cheap and definitive, so it is the whole sniff; a file failing it
        is not Selafin.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the endianness probe succeeds.
        """
        try:
            detect_endianness(path, expect_first_record=_TITLE_LENGTH)
        except ValueError:
            return False
        return True

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Selafin file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The Selafin file to read.
            lazy: When ``True``, leave each variable's slab behind a loader; when
                ``False``, read every value now.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, faces and the node-located variables.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file is not Selafin, declares a parallel
                sub-domain, or is truncated against the counts its header promises.
        """
        return _SelafinReader(path, lazy=lazy).build()

    def write(self, dataset, path: str, **options) -> None:
        """Write a mesh and its node-located results back to a Selafin file.

        Emits the same Fortran-record layout the reader parses, through
        :func:`write_selafin`: the title, the variable names, ``IPARAM``, the
        ``NELEM``/``NPOIN``/``NDP`` record, the ``IKLE`` connectivity (the base recorded
        on the mesh is re-applied, so a file read 1-based is written back 1-based),
        ``IPOBO``, the ``x``/``y`` node arrays, then one time record per step carrying each
        node-located variable's slab.

        Selafin stores one element width, so every face must share a vertex count; a
        mixed-width mesh is refused. Only node-located variables are written -- the format
        has no face-located storage. Coordinates and values are written at ``float64``
        (double precision) by default, so the round trip is lossless; pass
        ``precision="single"`` for the smaller, lossy ``float32`` layout.

        Args:
            dataset: The :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` to write.
            path: The output ``.slf`` path.
            **options: ``precision`` is ``"double"`` (default) or ``"single"``.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the dataset has no face connectivity, if its
                faces do not all share one vertex count (Selafin needs a uniform ``NDP``),
                or if ``precision`` is neither ``"single"`` nor ``"double"``.
        """
        mesh = dataset.mesh
        connectivity = getattr(mesh, "face_node_connectivity", None)
        if connectivity is None or connectivity.data is None:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"cannot write {path!r}: the dataset has no face connectivity to write "
                f"as a Selafin mesh"
            )
        faces = np.asarray(connectivity.data)
        base = connectivity.original_start_index
        if base is None:
            base = 1
        ikle = [[int(v) + base for v in row if int(v) != -1] for row in faces]
        widths = {len(row) for row in ikle}
        if len(widths) != 1:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"cannot write {path!r} to Selafin: every element must have the same node "
                f"count, but the mesh mixes widths {sorted(widths)}"
            )
        node_x = np.asarray(mesh.node_x, dtype=np.float64).tolist()
        node_y = np.asarray(mesh.node_y, dtype=np.float64).tolist()
        if "node_z" in dataset.data_variable_names:
            z = dataset.get("node_z")
            if z is not None and z.location == "node":
                warnings.warn(
                    "Selafin stores only node x/y, so the dataset's node_z (bed "
                    "elevation) is dropped on write; it is geometry, not a result series.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
        node_pairs = [
            (name, dataset.get(name))
            for name in dataset.data_variable_names
            if dataset.get(name).location == "node" and name != "node_z"
        ]
        names = [self._selafin_name(name, var.units) for name, var in node_pairs]
        if node_pairs:
            stamps = dataset.time_values
            times = (
                [float(t) for t in stamps]
                if stamps is not None and len(stamps)
                else [0.0]
            )
        else:
            times = []
        values = self._node_series(node_pairs, len(times))
        write_selafin(
            path,
            node_x=node_x,
            node_y=node_y,
            ikle=ikle,
            variable_names=names,
            times=times,
            values=values,
            double=self._resolve_precision(options.get("precision")),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _node_series(node_pairs, n_times: int) -> list:
        """Build the per-step value blocks for the node variables.

        Each 2-D (time-varying) variable must share the dataset's time axis; a static
        (1-D) field is repeated on every step. A variable whose own time axis differs is
        refused with a clear error rather than being silently truncated or index-erroring.

        Args:
            node_pairs: ``(name, variable)`` pairs of the node-located variables to write.
            n_times: The dataset's time-step count (the shared Selafin time axis).

        Returns:
            list: One block per time step, each a list of per-variable node value lists.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If a time-varying variable's first-axis length is
                not ``n_times``.
        """
        prepared = []
        for name, var in node_pairs:
            array = np.asarray(var.data, dtype=np.float64)
            if array.ndim == 2 and array.shape[0] != n_times:
                raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                    f"cannot write node variable {name!r} to Selafin: its time axis has "
                    f"{array.shape[0]} steps but the dataset's is {n_times}"
                )
            prepared.append(array)
        return [
            [(array[step] if array.ndim == 2 else array).tolist() for array in prepared]
            for step in range(n_times)
        ]

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_precision(precision) -> bool:
        """Resolve the ``precision`` option to the double-precision flag ``write_selafin`` takes.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` for double (the default, lossless), ``False`` for single.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: On any value other than ``"single"``/``"double"``.
        """
        if precision in (None, "double"):
            return True
        if precision == "single":
            return False
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"unknown Selafin precision {precision!r}; use 'single' or 'double'"
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _selafin_name(name: str, units) -> str:
        """Pack a variable name and unit into the 32-character Selafin name record.

        The first 16 characters are the name, the next 16 the unit, each space-padded and
        truncated -- the inverse of the reader's by-position split.
        """
        label = f"{name[:_NAME_HALF]:<{_NAME_HALF}}"
        unit = f"{(units or '')[:_NAME_HALF]:<{_NAME_HALF}}"
        return label + unit

docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    Args:

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> UgridDataset | Network1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Network1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: write(dataset, path, **options)
docs.text:
Write a mesh and its node-located results back to a Selafin file.

Emits the same Fortran-record layout the reader parses, through :func:write_selafin: the title, the variable names, IPARAM, the NELEM/NPOIN/NDP record, the IKLE connectivity (the base recorded on the mesh is re-applied, so a file read 1-based is written back 1-based), IPOBO, the x/y node arrays, then one time record per step carrying each node-located variable's slab.

Selafin stores one element width, so every face must share a vertex count; a mixed-width mesh is refused. Only node-located variables are written -- the format has no face-located storage. Coordinates and values are written at float64 (double precision) by default, so the round trip is lossless; pass precision="single" for the smaller, lossy float32 layout.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset

The :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset to write.

required path str

The output .slf path.

required **options

precision is "double" (default) or "single".

{}

Raises:

Type Description FileFormatNotSupportedError

If the dataset has no face connectivity, if its faces do not all share one vertex count (Selafin needs a uniform NDP), or if precision is neither "single" nor "double".

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/drivers/telemac.py 
def write(self, dataset, path: str, **options) -> None:
    """Write a mesh and its node-located results back to a Selafin file.

    Emits the same Fortran-record layout the reader parses, through
    :func:`write_selafin`: the title, the variable names, ``IPARAM``, the
    ``NELEM``/``NPOIN``/``NDP`` record, the ``IKLE`` connectivity (the base recorded
    on the mesh is re-applied, so a file read 1-based is written back 1-based),
    ``IPOBO``, the ``x``/``y`` node arrays, then one time record per step carrying each
    node-located variable's slab.

    Selafin stores one element width, so every face must share a vertex count; a
    mixed-width mesh is refused. Only node-located variables are written -- the format
    has no face-located storage. Coordinates and values are written at ``float64``
    (double precision) by default, so the round trip is lossless; pass
    ``precision="single"`` for the smaller, lossy ``float32`` layout.

    Args:
        dataset: The :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` to write.
        path: The output ``.slf`` path.
        **options: ``precision`` is ``"double"`` (default) or ``"single"``.

    Raises:
        FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the dataset has no face connectivity, if its
            faces do not all share one vertex count (Selafin needs a uniform ``NDP``),
            or if ``precision`` is neither ``"single"`` nor ``"double"``.
    """
    mesh = dataset.mesh
    connectivity = getattr(mesh, "face_node_connectivity", None)
    if connectivity is None or connectivity.data is None:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r}: the dataset has no face connectivity to write "
            f"as a Selafin mesh"
        )
    faces = np.asarray(connectivity.data)
    base = connectivity.original_start_index
    if base is None:
        base = 1
    ikle = [[int(v) + base for v in row if int(v) != -1] for row in faces]
    widths = {len(row) for row in ikle}
    if len(widths) != 1:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r} to Selafin: every element must have the same node "
            f"count, but the mesh mixes widths {sorted(widths)}"
        )
    node_x = np.asarray(mesh.node_x, dtype=np.float64).tolist()
    node_y = np.asarray(mesh.node_y, dtype=np.float64).tolist()
    if "node_z" in dataset.data_variable_names:
        z = dataset.get("node_z")
        if z is not None and z.location == "node":
            warnings.warn(
                "Selafin stores only node x/y, so the dataset's node_z (bed "
                "elevation) is dropped on write; it is geometry, not a result series.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
    node_pairs = [
        (name, dataset.get(name))
        for name in dataset.data_variable_names
        if dataset.get(name).location == "node" and name != "node_z"
    ]
    names = [self._selafin_name(name, var.units) for name, var in node_pairs]
    if node_pairs:
        stamps = dataset.time_values
        times = (
            [float(t) for t in stamps]
            if stamps is not None and len(stamps)
            else [0.0]
        )
    else:
        times = []
    values = self._node_series(node_pairs, len(times))
    write_selafin(
        path,
        node_x=node_x,
        node_y=node_y,
        ikle=ikle,
        variable_names=names,
        times=times,
        values=values,
        double=self._resolve_precision(options.get("precision")),
    )

docs.title: SRH-2D
docs.text:
Reader for the SRH-2D (USBR/Aquaveo) ASCII mesh format (task C12).

An SRH-2D model stores its mesh as a trio of ASCII files sharing one basename stem. This driver is the geometry/control reader; it reads the first and consults the other two for metadata:

  • <case>.srhgeom — the mesh. Elem <id> n1 n2 n3[ n4 …] lines carry mixed triangle/quad/polygon faces by 1-based node id, and Node <id> x y z lines the node coordinates and bed elevation. The Name, GridUnit and NodeString cards are read for metadata only.
  • <case>.srhhydro — the control deck: Grid "<case>.srhgeom", HydroMat "<case>.srhmat", ManningsN <material-id> <n>, BC and SimTime.
  • <case>.srhmat — the element-to-material-zone map, one Material <id> <elem …> block per zone (element ids continue onto the following unprefixed lines).
Driver name srh2d Suffixes .srhgeom, .srhhydro (either member of the trio) Capabilities read_mesh

docs.title: Dispatch
docs.text:
Point read_file at either the .srhgeom or the .srhhydro; the driver resolves the rest of the trio from the Grid / HydroMat cards, falling back to the shared basename stem:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("Muncie.srhgeom", driver="srh2d")
elevation = mesh.get("node_z")      # node-located bed elevation
zone = mesh.get("material")         # face-located material-zone id

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The input is a file set. A .srhhydro whose geometry cannot be resolved (no Grid card and no <stem>.srhgeom sibling) is declined by can_open.
  • Faces are mixed-width polygons. Triangles, quads and larger polygons share one fill-padded connectivity array; short rows are padded with -1.
  • Node and element ids are resolved through an id map, so a gapped or out-of-order file stays correctly wired rather than assuming id == index + 1. The ids are 1-based, which is recorded for a writer to restore.
  • Bed elevation becomes a node_z variable, since the pyramids mesh model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate.
  • Material and Manning's n are carried only when clean. The material face variable is attached when the .srhmat assigns every element exactly one known zone; the manning_n face variable is attached on top of that when every assigned zone has a ManningsN value in the .srhhydro. An inconsistent or incomplete map is dropped rather than guessed.
  • Results are not read here. SRH-2D writes its results as XMDF or VTK, which the xmdf and VTK drivers already read; this is the geometry/control reader.
  • SRH-2D carries no CRS, so crs is always None. The GridUnit card is recorded as a grid_unit global attribute but never interpreted as a projection.

docs.title: STL — stereolithography
docs.text:
The STL reader. ASCII (solid/facet/outer loop/vertex/endloop/endfacet) and binary (80-byte header, a uint32 triangle count, then 50 bytes per triangle), hand-parsed — a triangle-soup geometry format with elevation per vertex and no time axis.

No CRS, no georeferencing. STL carries no coordinate reference system or spatial reference of any kind, so crs is always None. That makes it a low-value format for a GIS stack; it is provided for mesh interchange only.

Driver name stl Suffixes .stl Capabilities read_mesh, read_data Extra required none Returns UgridDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("solid.stl")

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• STL has no vertex indexing. Every triangle stores its three corner coordinates inline, so the reader welds byte-identical vertices into a shared node list and rebuilds the triangle face connectivity against it.
  • ASCII and binary are both supported. The two are told apart by the binary size identity (80 + 4 + 50 × count), not by the leading word — a binary STL's header very often begins with solid too, which naive detection mistakes for ASCII.
  • A round trip is not geometrically faithful. z survives as a node_z variable, but pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the geometry sees the (x, y) projection — and a 3D solid's vertical faces collapse to zero-area (degenerate) faces in that projection (design §6).
  • STL carries no CRS and no georeferencing, so crs is None.
  • The whole file is read eagerly, so the driver does not declare lazy_data.
  • The per-triangle normal and the 2-byte attribute word are read for width but not carried.
  • Welded vertices are 0-based and stay so.

docs.title: pyramids_mesh.drivers.stl.StlDriver
docs.text:
Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the STL (stereolithography) format, ASCII and binary.

STL stores a flat list of triangles, each carrying its three corner coordinates inline with no shared vertex table. The reader welds byte-identical vertices into one node list and rebuilds the triangle face connectivity against it, so a closed solid comes back as a proper indexed mesh rather than a triangle soup.

Documented limitations
  • A round trip is not geometrically faithful. z survives as a node_z variable, but pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the geometry sees the (x, y) projection -- and a 3D solid's vertical faces collapse to zero-area (degenerate) faces in that projection (design section 6).
  • STL carries no CRS or georeferencing, so crs is None. This makes it a low-value format for a GIS stack; it is provided for interchange only.
  • The whole file is read eagerly, so the driver does not declare lazy_data.
  • The per-triangle normal and the 2-byte attribute word are read for width but not carried; the mesh model has no place for either.
  • Welded vertices are 0-based, as pyramids expects, and stay so.

Examples:

  • Write a tiny two-triangle ASCII STL and read it back. The shared corner is welded, so the unit square comes back as four nodes and two faces:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh.drivers.stl import StlDriver lines = ( ... "solid square", ... "facet normal 0 0 1", ... " outer loop", ... " vertex 0 0 0", ... " vertex 1 0 0", ... " vertex 1 1 0", ... " endloop", ... " endfacet", ... "facet normal 0 0 1", ... " outer loop", ... " vertex 0 0 0", ... " vertex 1 1 0", ... " vertex 0 1 0", ... " endloop", ... " endfacet", ... "endsolid square", ... ) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "square.stl") ... with open(path, "w", encoding="ascii") as handle: ... for line in lines: ... print(line, file=handle) ... dataset = StlDriver().read(path) dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (4, 2) dataset.mesh.crs is None True

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/drivers/stl.py 
class StlDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the STL (stereolithography) format, ASCII and binary.

    STL stores a flat list of triangles, each carrying its three corner coordinates
    inline with no shared vertex table. The reader welds byte-identical vertices into one
    node list and rebuilds the triangle face connectivity against it, so a closed solid
    comes back as a proper indexed mesh rather than a triangle soup.

    Documented limitations:
        - **A round trip is not geometrically faithful.** ``z`` survives as a ``node_z``
          variable, but pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the
          geometry sees the ``(x, y)`` projection -- and a 3D solid's vertical faces
          collapse to zero-area (degenerate) faces in that projection (design section 6).
        - **STL carries no CRS or georeferencing**, so ``crs`` is ``None``. This makes it
          a low-value format for a GIS stack; it is provided for interchange only.
        - **The whole file is read eagerly**, so the driver does not declare ``lazy_data``.
        - The per-triangle normal and the 2-byte attribute word are read for width but
          not carried; the mesh model has no place for either.
        - Welded vertices are 0-based, as pyramids expects, and stay so.

    Examples:
        - Write a tiny two-triangle ASCII STL and read it back. The shared corner is
          welded, so the unit square comes back as four nodes and two faces:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.stl import StlDriver
            >>> lines = (
            ...     "solid square",
            ...     "facet normal 0 0 1",
            ...     " outer loop",
            ...     "  vertex 0 0 0",
            ...     "  vertex 1 0 0",
            ...     "  vertex 1 1 0",
            ...     " endloop",
            ...     " endfacet",
            ...     "facet normal 0 0 1",
            ...     " outer loop",
            ...     "  vertex 0 0 0",
            ...     "  vertex 1 1 0",
            ...     "  vertex 0 1 0",
            ...     " endloop",
            ...     " endfacet",
            ...     "endsolid square",
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "square.stl")
            ...     with open(path, "w", encoding="ascii") as handle:
            ...         for line in lines:
            ...             print(line, file=handle)
            ...     dataset = StlDriver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (4, 2)
            >>> dataset.mesh.crs is None
            True
    """

    name = "stl"
    long_name = "STL (stereolithography)"
    suffixes = (".stl",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is a size-consistent binary or an ASCII STL.

        Binary is tested first and by size, not by the leading word: a binary STL's
        header often starts with ``solid`` too, so only the ``80 + 4 + 50 * count`` size
        identity tells the two apart reliably. Never raises -- an unreadable file is
        reported as not an STL.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` for a size-consistent binary STL or an ASCII ``solid``/``facet``
                file.
        """
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - can_open checks isfile first
            return False
        if _binary_triangle_count(raw) is not None:
            return True
        return _looks_ascii(raw)

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read an STL file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The STL file to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- the whole file is read eagerly.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Welded nodes, triangle faces and the ``node_z`` elevation.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: On a file that is neither a size-consistent
                binary STL nor an ASCII ``solid``/``facet`` file, a facet without exactly
                three vertices, or a non-numeric coordinate.
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
        count = _binary_triangle_count(raw)
        if count is not None:
            if count == 0:
                raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                    f"{path!r} is an empty binary STL (zero triangles); it carries no "
                    f"surface to build a mesh from"
                )
            triangles = _read_binary_triangles(raw, count)
        elif _looks_ascii(raw):
            triangles = _read_ascii_triangles(raw, path)
        else:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"{path!r} is not a readable STL: it is neither a size-consistent "
                f"binary STL (an 80-byte header, a uint32 triangle count and 50 bytes "
                f"per triangle) nor an ASCII 'solid'/'facet' file"
            )
        return _weld(triangles, path)

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/_base.py 
def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override
    this to read the names from the file.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

    Examples:
        - A single-mesh driver names one topology, so the list it returns is the
          set of values ``read``'s ``mesh_name`` will accept:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> TinyDriver().mesh_names("anything.tiny")
            ['mesh2d']
    """
    return [self._default_mesh_name]

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Network1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description UgridDataset | Network1d

UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/_base.py 
def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> UgridDataset | Network1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.UgridDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Network1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        UgridDataset | Network1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: SU2 — .su2 native mesh
docs.text:
The SU2 reader. SU2 is the native ASCII mesh of the SU2 open-source CFD/multiphysics suite: a flat, section-keyed text file holding a dimension card, a VTK-typed interior element table, a node table, and named boundary markers.

Driver name su2 Suffixes .su2 Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns UgridDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("domain.su2")   # resolved to this package's su2 driver
mesh.mesh.n_face

docs.title: File shape
docs.text:
NDIME= 2                      dimension: 2 or 3
NELEM= 25                     interior element table
 9  0  1  7  6  0             <vtk-type> n1 n2 … [element-id]
 …
NPOIN= 36                     node coordinates
 0.0  0.0  0                  x y [z] [point-id]
 …
NMARK= 4                      boundary markers
MARKER_TAG= bottom
MARKER_ELEMS= 5
 3  0  1                      line/edge elements (VTK type 3)
 …

The VTK cell codes are triangle 5, quadrilateral 9, line 3, tetra 10 and hexa 12. A node table row indexes nodes directly — SU2 is 0-based.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Surface meshes only. Triangle (code 5) and quadrilateral (code 9) elements become the fill-padded face_node_connectivity; a mixed-width file pads the short rows with -1. A volume element type (tetra 10, hexa 12, or any other 3D cell) in the NELEM table is refused rather than flattened to a face — there is no committed 3D sample to validate such a read against.
  • 0-based, no id map. SU2 element rows index the node table directly, so the connectivity is already 0-based: start_index and original_start_index are both 0 and the validator subtracts nothing. The optional trailing element/point index column each row may carry is ignored, exactly as SU2 ignores it on read.
  • Boundary markers are metadata, not topology. Each MARKER_TAG group is recorded as su2_markers on the global attributes (tag → boundary-element count); the marker edges are not built into a separate 1D network.
  • No CRS. SU2 carries no coordinate-reference declaration, so crs is None and is never guessed from the coordinate magnitudes.
